description: A small agent that gives a local Ollama model two date tools, runs the tool the model asks for, feeds the result back, and returns the model's final answer.

steps.description: The script imports `json` and `requests` to call the local model, and `date` from `datetime` for the two date tools.

Two plain functions do the real work. `get_today` returns today's date as a string, and `days_until` parses an ISO date and returns the number of days as a string. If the date will not parse, `days_until` prints a labeled error, prints the traceback, and returns `error: bad date`.

`TOOLS` lists the two functions as schemas the model can call. Each has a name, a description that tells the model when to reach for it, and a `parameters` object. `days_until` requires one string argument, `target_iso`, described as a date in `YYYY-MM-DD` form.
`REGISTRY` maps each tool name to its Python function, so the agent can turn a name the model returns back into a real call.

`agent` seeds the message list with the user's question, then loops up to `max_steps` times. Each turn posts to `http://localhost:11434/api/chat` with model `qwen2.5:3b`, `stream` off, the `TOOLS` list, `temperature` 0.0, `seed` 42, and the running messages, then reads the `message` field from the reply.
The model's message is appended to the conversation, then the code reads `tool_calls`. When there are none, the model has answered, so `agent` returns the message content.

For each tool call it takes the function name and arguments, looks the name up in `REGISTRY`, and calls it, falling back to `unknown tool` for a name that is not registered. It prints a `[tool]` line and appends the result as a `tool` message, so the model sees the answer on the next turn.

steps.answer: The `for` loop runs at most `max_steps` turns, and then `agent` returns `step budget exceeded`. A model that never settles on an answer cannot make the agent run forever.
steps.question: What happens if the model keeps asking for tools and never gives a final answer?

steps.description: The final line asks how many days until the last day of classes, December 7, 2026. The run prints one `[tool]` line, `[tool] days_until({'target_iso': '2026-12-07'}) -> 23`, then the answer that there are 23 days until December 7, 2026.

title: A Two-Tool Date Agent
